report.incidentSummary: Starting at 14:20 IST (08:50 UTC) on 2026-09-25, the AI assistant began responding to some users that they had no holdings, despite the Portfolio screen displaying their investments accurately. An upstream transient timeout spike in user-context-service between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC triggered a fallback mechanism that wrote empty context records (holdings=0, sips=0) into the cache with an excessively long 6-hour TTL (21600s). Although user-context-service timeouts and latency normalized by 09:25 UTC and portfolio-service remained healthy throughout, affected users continued reading poisoned cache entries, keeping missing_context_rate elevated at ~8% through 11:45 UTC.
report.rootCauseStatement: During a transient surge in context build timeouts between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC, user-context-service fell back to writing empty context entries (holdings=0, sips=0) into the cache with an excessively long 6-hour TTL (21600s). Subsequent assistant requests for affected users hit these poisoned cache records, causing persistent holdings omission in chat even after underlying services recovered.

hypotheses.cause: During transient context build timeouts, user-context-service fell back to caching empty context entries (holdings=0, sips=0) with an excessively long 6-hour (21600s) TTL, causing persistent holdings omission for affected users.
hypotheses.rationale: Logs directly confirm that when context builds timed out starting at 08:50:03 UTC, user-context-service wrote 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'. While error rates, timeouts, and latency returned to baseline by 09:25 UTC, missing_context_rate remained plateaued at ~8% through 11:45 UTC because affected users continued serving from the poisoned 6-hour cache entries.

hypotheses.cause: Ongoing capacity saturation or pod unreadiness in user-context-service caused persistent context build failures.
hypotheses.rationale: User-context-service error rate, timeout count, and p95 latency completely recovered to baseline levels by 09:25 UTC, and upstream portfolio-service remained healthy with a flat error rate of ~0.20%. Persistent missing context at ~8% hours after full recovery contradicts ongoing capacity saturation as the primary cause.

hypotheses.cause: Knowledge-index release CHG-48223 at 08:45 UTC altered search ranking or document payloads, causing assistant context truncation.
hypotheses.rationale: Assistant-orchestrator error rate and p95 latency remained flat and healthy at baseline throughout the window. Holdings context is fetched exclusively from user-context-service, and explicit poisoned cache logs in user-context-service account for the exact symptoms.

facts.statement: user-context-service experienced a sharp spike in error rate (peaking at 10.32% at 09:05 UTC) and timeout count (peaking at 37.58/min at 08:55 UTC), which recovered to baseline levels by 09:25 UTC.
user-context-service missing_context_rate jumped from ~0.8% baseline to 12.0% at 08:50 UTC, peaked at 20.46% at 09:05 UTC, and remained persistently elevated at 7.0%-8.7% through 11:45 UTC.
portfolio-service maintained a stable baseline error rate of ~0.20% with no elevation throughout the investigation window (08:15 to 11:45 UTC).
user-context-service logged 193 instances of 'context build timed out after #ms (holdings fetch pending); # of # pods ready' between 08:50:18 UTC and 09:21:58 UTC.
Starting at 08:50:03.686 UTC, user-context-service repeatedly executed log events matching 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'.
cache hit rate for the user_context keyspace rose from ~95% to ~98.5%-99% starting around 09:00 UTC and remained elevated through 11:45 UTC, while other keyspaces remained at normal ~94% hit rates.
assistant-orchestrator error rate (0.45%-0.57%) and p95 latency (6018-6724 ms) remained steady at normal baseline across the entire window.
No deployments or configuration changes were executed on assistant-orchestrator, user-context-service, portfolio-service, or cache on 2026-09-25.

inferences.statement: During the transient timeout storm (08:50-09:22 UTC), user-context-service poisoned the cache by storing empty holdings with a 6-hour TTL for users whose context build timed out.
The ongoing ~8% missing_context_rate and the persistent assistant reports of no holdings after 09:25 UTC are sustained entirely by repeated cache hits on the poisoned 21600s TTL entries.
Assistant-orchestrator did not register errors because it received valid 200 responses containing empty context and gracefully answered users that they held no funds.

assumptions.statement: The assistant orchestrator relies entirely on user-context-service for holdings data rather than querying portfolio-service directly.
Cached user context keys are not automatically evicted or invalidated upon portfolio-service updates in the absence of explicit eviction triggers.

timeline.event: Routine deployment CHG-48223 to knowledge-index completed.
user-context-service latency and timeouts surge; first poisoned empty context written to cache with 21600s TTL at 08:50:03.686 UTC.
user-context-service errors (10.32%) and missing_context_rate (20.46%) peak; user_context cache hit rate rises to ~99%.
user-context-service timeouts and latency recover to baseline; context build timeout warnings cease.
missing_context_rate remains plateaued at ~8% as affected users continue hitting poisoned cache entries.
Support team reports persistent assistant claims of zero holdings (INC-3320).

confidence.rationale: Log evidence directly records user-context-service writing fallback cache entries with 'holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s' at the exact onset of the incident. This matches the discrepancy between a healthy Portfolio screen and persistent assistant failures well after latency normalized.

gaps.description: Specific pod readiness and scaling logs for user-context-service during 08:50-09:22 UTC were not retrieved due to query budget limits.
gaps.impact: The exact root trigger of the transient context build timeout surge (e.g., pod restart or thread starvation) is not definitively proven, though the mechanism of persistent failure via poisoned caching is fully established.

recommendedActions.action: Flush or selectively invalidate all user_ctx:* keys in the cache user_context keyspace that were populated between 08:50 and 09:25 UTC.
recommendedActions.rationale: Immediate remediation to purge poisoned empty context records with 6-hour TTLs and force fresh context builds from portfolio-service.
recommendedActions.verification: Confirm that missing_context_rate on user-context-service drops from ~8% back to baseline (<1.0%) and cache hit rate normalizes to ~95%.

recommendedActions.action: Modify user-context-service fallback behavior to use a short negative-cache TTL (e.g., 30-60 seconds) or avoid caching degraded empty context on upstream timeouts.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents transient downstream or intra-service timeouts from causing multi-hour persistent outages for affected users.
recommendedActions.verification: Run a staging test simulating a portfolio-service timeout and verify that subsequent cache entries expire within 60 seconds.

recommendedActions.action: Investigate user-context-service pod readiness probes and resource limits during the 08:50-09:22 UTC window to prevent future context build timeout spikes.
recommendedActions.rationale: Address the underlying reason why pods experienced timeout spikes and unreadiness warnings.
recommendedActions.verification: Review Kubernetes event logs and CPU/memory throttling metrics during the incident window.

findings.summary: During 08:50-09:22 UTC, user-context-service suffered a temporary burst of timeouts while fetching holdings, causing error_rate to spike to ~10.3%. On timeout, user-context-service fell back to writing empty context ('holdings=0 sips=0') into cache with a 6-hour TTL (21600s). Portfolio-service itself remained healthy (error_rate ~0.20%), and cache keyspaces were healthy. Because of the 6-hour TTL on poisoned cache entries, affected users continue to read empty holdings from cache, keeping missing_context_rate elevated at ~8%.

observations.statement: user-context-service experienced a sharp spike in error_rate between 08:50:00Z and 09:20:00Z (rising from baseline ~0.3% to a peak of 10.32% at 09:05:00Z before recovering by 09:25:00Z), while missing_context_rate spiked from ~0.8% to 20.46% at 09:05:00Z and remained elevated at ~8% through the rest of the window.
portfolio-service showed a completely flat error_rate (~0.20% baseline) throughout the investigation window (08:15:00Z to 11:45:00Z), with no elevated error rate detected globally.

cache hit rates across factsheets, nav, prices, and sessions keyspaces remained normal and stable (~94%), while cache hit rate for the user_context keyspace rose from ~95% to ~98.5-99% starting around 09:00:00Z and remained elevated.

Between 08:50:18Z and 09:21:58Z, user-context-service logged warnings: 'context build timed out after #ms (holdings fetch pending); # of # pods ready' and subsequently wrote fallback empty contexts to cache: 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'.

During the timeout window (08:50-09:22 UTC), user-context-service cached empty holdings (holdings=0) with a long TTL of 21600s (6 hours) in the cache user_context keyspace. Even after timeouts stopped around 09:22 UTC, subsequent queries for those affected users hit the poisoned cache entries, explaining why missing_context_rate stayed at ~8% and users continue to see no holdings while Portfolio screen works normally.

findings.summary: No deployments or configuration changes were made to assistant-orchestrator, user-context-service, portfolio-service, or cache on 2026-09-25; the last changes were minor routine releases on 2026-09-24. However, a release was applied to upstream dependency knowledge-index at 08:45 UTC (CHG-48223, version 1.9.0 hybrid search ranking), 5 minutes before the reported onset. Past incidents show no identical precedent of assistant holdings omission, pointing to either a runtime user-context-service degradation/cache issue or context interference from the knowledge-index deployment.

observations.statement: No deployments, configuration updates, or feature flag changes were applied to assistant-orchestrator, user-context-service, portfolio-service, or cache during 2026-09-25. The most recent changes for these services occurred on 2026-09-24 (CHG-48518 log shipper upgrade on user-context-service at 11:38 UTC and CHG-48527 release 0.42.1 on assistant-orchestrator at 11:41 UTC).

A deployment occurred at 2026-09-25T08:45:00.000Z to knowledge-index (CHG-48223, version 1.8.0 -> 1.9.0, 'release: hybrid search ranking'), approximately 5 minutes prior to the reported incident onset at ~08:50 UTC.

assistant-orchestrator depends synchronously on knowledge-index (timeout 800ms, retries 0) and user-context-service (timeout 1200ms, retries 0); user-context-service depends synchronously on portfolio-service (timeout 1000ms, retries 0) and cache (timeout 50ms, retries 0).

Past incidents in related services include PIR-1555 (LLM provider outage/timeouts), PIR-1114 (wrong index content), PIR-1375 (DB VACUUM elevating portfolio-service latency to 900ms), PIR-1411 (compliance filter false positive), and PIR-1594 (cache failover invalidating sessions). None match a scenario where the assistant specifically fails to recognize user holdings while portfolio screen functions normally.

Because no changes were made to assistant-orchestrator, user-context-service, portfolio-service, or cache, the issue is likely due to an upstream failure in user-context-service (e.g. cache or portfolio-service read timeout/failure returning empty context), prompt size/format changes following the 08:45 UTC knowledge-index hybrid search release displacing user context, or cache eviction of user context.

# Investigation report: Assistant cannot see user holdings

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** critic_accepted · **Confidence:** 0.88 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
Starting at 14:20 IST (08:50 UTC) on 2026-09-25, the AI assistant began responding to some users that they had no holdings, despite the Portfolio screen displaying their investments accurately. An upstream transient timeout spike in user-context-service between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC triggered a fallback mechanism that wrote empty context records (holdings=0, sips=0) into the cache with an excessively long 6-hour TTL (21600s). Although user-context-service timeouts and latency normalized by 09:25 UTC and portfolio-service remained healthy throughout, affected users continued reading poisoned cache entries, keeping missing_context_rate elevated at ~8% through 11:45 UTC.

**Root cause:** During a transient surge in context build timeouts between 08:50 and 09:22 UTC, user-context-service fell back to writing empty context entries (holdings=0, sips=0) into the cache with an excessively long 6-hour TTL (21600s). Subsequent assistant requests for affected users hit these poisoned cache records, causing persistent holdings omission in chat even after underlying services recovered.

## Hypotheses
1. **During transient context build timeouts, user-context-service fell back to caching empty context entries (holdings=0, sips=0) with an excessively long 6-hour (21600s) TTL, causing persistent holdings omission for affected users.** — `user-context-service`, cache_or_staleness, confidence 0.88, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_2, ev_3, ev_6, ev_10, ev_11, ev_15, ev_17] · Contradicting: none
   - Logs directly confirm that when context builds timed out starting at 08:50:03 UTC, user-context-service wrote 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'. While error rates, timeouts, and latency returned to baseline by 09:25 UTC, missing_context_rate remained plateaued at ~8% through 11:45 UTC because affected users continued serving from the poisoned 6-hour cache entries.
2. **Ongoing capacity saturation or pod unreadiness in user-context-service caused persistent context build failures.** — `user-context-service`, capacity_saturation, confidence 0.30, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_10, ev_11, ev_17] · Contradicting: [ev_1, ev_2, ev_7, ev_11, ev_17]
   - User-context-service error rate, timeout count, and p95 latency completely recovered to baseline levels by 09:25 UTC, and upstream portfolio-service remained healthy with a flat error rate of ~0.20%. Persistent missing context at ~8% hours after full recovery contradicts ongoing capacity saturation as the primary cause.
3. **Knowledge-index release CHG-48223 at 08:45 UTC altered search ranking or document payloads, causing assistant context truncation.** — `knowledge-index`, deployment_regression, confidence 0.10, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_9, ev_12] · Contradicting: [ev_10, ev_13, ev_15, ev_18]
   - Assistant-orchestrator error rate and p95 latency remained flat and healthy at baseline throughout the window. Holdings context is fetched exclusively from user-context-service, and explicit poisoned cache logs in user-context-service account for the exact symptoms.

## Facts
- user-context-service experienced a sharp spike in error rate (peaking at 10.32% at 09:05 UTC) and timeout count (peaking at 37.58/min at 08:55 UTC), which recovered to baseline levels by 09:25 UTC. [ev_1, ev_11]
- user-context-service missing_context_rate jumped from ~0.8% baseline to 12.0% at 08:50 UTC, peaked at 20.46% at 09:05 UTC, and remained persistently elevated at 7.0%-8.7% through 11:45 UTC. [ev_2, ev_3]
- portfolio-service maintained a stable baseline error rate of ~0.20% with no elevation throughout the investigation window (08:15 to 11:45 UTC). [ev_7]
- user-context-service logged 193 instances of 'context build timed out after #ms (holdings fetch pending); # of # pods ready' between 08:50:18 UTC and 09:21:58 UTC. [ev_10]
- Starting at 08:50:03.686 UTC, user-context-service repeatedly executed log events matching 'cache SET user_ctx:u_<id> holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s (fallback after timeout)'. [ev_10, ev_15]
- cache hit rate for the user_context keyspace rose from ~95% to ~98.5%-99% starting around 09:00 UTC and remained elevated through 11:45 UTC, while other keyspaces remained at normal ~94% hit rates. [ev_6]
- assistant-orchestrator error rate (0.45%-0.57%) and p95 latency (6018-6724 ms) remained steady at normal baseline across the entire window. [ev_13, ev_18]
- No deployments or configuration changes were executed on assistant-orchestrator, user-context-service, portfolio-service, or cache on 2026-09-25. [ev_5]

## Inferences
- During the transient timeout storm (08:50-09:22 UTC), user-context-service poisoned the cache by storing empty holdings with a 6-hour TTL for users whose context build timed out. [ev_1, ev_10, ev_11, ev_15]
- The ongoing ~8% missing_context_rate and the persistent assistant reports of no holdings after 09:25 UTC are sustained entirely by repeated cache hits on the poisoned 21600s TTL entries. [ev_2, ev_6, ev_15]
- Assistant-orchestrator did not register errors because it received valid 200 responses containing empty context and gracefully answered users that they held no funds. [ev_12, ev_13, ev_18]

## Assumptions
- The assistant orchestrator relies entirely on user-context-service for holdings data rather than querying portfolio-service directly.
- Cached user context keys are not automatically evicted or invalidated upon portfolio-service updates in the absence of explicit eviction triggers.

## Timeline
- **2026-09-25 14:15 IST (08:45 UTC)** Routine deployment CHG-48223 to knowledge-index completed. [ev_9]
- **2026-09-25 14:20 IST (08:50 UTC)** user-context-service latency and timeouts surge; first poisoned empty context written to cache with 21600s TTL at 08:50:03.686 UTC. [ev_1, ev_11, ev_15, ev_17]
- **2026-09-25 14:35 IST (09:05 UTC)** user-context-service errors (10.32%) and missing_context_rate (20.46%) peak; user_context cache hit rate rises to ~99%. [ev_1, ev_2, ev_6]
- **2026-09-25 14:55 IST (09:25 UTC)** user-context-service timeouts and latency recover to baseline; context build timeout warnings cease. [ev_1, ev_10, ev_11, ev_17]
- **2026-09-25 15:00 - 17:15 IST (09:30 - 11:45 UTC)** missing_context_rate remains plateaued at ~8% as affected users continue hitting poisoned cache entries. [ev_2, ev_3, ev_6]
- **2026-09-25 16:30 IST (11:00 UTC)** Support team reports persistent assistant claims of zero holdings (INC-3320). [ev_2]

## Confidence
0.88: Log evidence directly records user-context-service writing fallback cache entries with 'holdings=0 sips=0 ttl=21600s' at the exact onset of the incident. This matches the discrepancy between a healthy Portfolio screen and persistent assistant failures well after latency normalized.

## Gaps
- Specific pod readiness and scaling logs for user-context-service during 08:50-09:22 UTC were not retrieved due to query budget limits. (impact: The exact root trigger of the transient context build timeout surge (e.g., pod restart or thread starvation) is not definitively proven, though the mechanism of persistent failure via poisoned caching is fully established.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Flush or selectively invalidate all user_ctx:* keys in the cache user_context keyspace that were populated between 08:50 and 09:25 UTC. [ev_2, ev_6, ev_15]
  - Why: Immediate remediation to purge poisoned empty context records with 6-hour TTLs and force fresh context builds from portfolio-service.
  - Verify: Confirm that missing_context_rate on user-context-service drops from ~8% back to baseline (<1.0%) and cache hit rate normalizes to ~95%.
- **[next]** Modify user-context-service fallback behavior to use a short negative-cache TTL (e.g., 30-60 seconds) or avoid caching degraded empty context on upstream timeouts. [ev_10, ev_15]
  - Why: Prevents transient downstream or intra-service timeouts from causing multi-hour persistent outages for affected users.
  - Verify: Run a staging test simulating a portfolio-service timeout and verify that subsequent cache entries expire within 60 seconds.
- **[later]** Investigate user-context-service pod readiness probes and resource limits during the 08:50-09:22 UTC window to prevent future context build timeout spikes. [ev_10, ev_11, ev_17]
  - Why: Address the underlying reason why pods experienced timeout spikes and unreadiness warnings.
  - Verify: Review Kubernetes event logs and CPU/memory throttling metrics during the incident window.
